title: Demonstrationes circa residua ex divisione potestatum per numeros primos resultantia

deep.reconstruction: Context: E449 is Euler's 1774 attempt to prove that every prime P has a primitive root, i.e. some a whose powers 1, a, a^2, ... run through all P-1 nonzero residues (announced in Scholion 37 and Theorem 38 on the next page). On the previous page Euler gives each 'formula' x^n - 1 n abstract 'cases' (roots). The 'proper cases' (casus proprii) of x^n - 1 are those roots that satisfy no x^d - 1 with d a proper divisor of n. He finds them recursively: proper(n) = n - sum of proper(d) over proper divisors d of n. In modern terms this is the identity sum_{d|n} N(d) = n, solved by inclusion-exclusion (Möbius inversion). On this page he tabulates the recursion for prime powers and products of distinct primes alpha, beta, gamma: p-1, p(p-1), (p-1)(q-1), alpha^2(alpha-1), alpha(alpha-1)(beta-1). He infers that for n = alpha^lambda beta^mu gamma^nu the count is alpha^{lambda-1}(alpha-1) beta^{mu-1}(beta-1) gamma^{nu-1}(gamma-1). He recognizes this as the number of integers below n coprime to n, i.e. phi(n). So he has, in effect, sum_{d|n} phi(d) = n, and phi(n) is the number of primitive n-th roots of unity (the degree of the n-th cyclotomic polynomial). Coroll. 1 (§35) applies this modulo P with n = P-1. Since x^{P-1} - 1 has P-1 real cases mod P (Fermat: every x = 1..P-1 works), the proper cases that remain after removing those shared with simpler formulas are all real. Coroll. 2 (§36) concludes that numbers below P always exist that satisfy x^{P-1} ≡ 1 and no lower x^d ≡ 1, i.e. primitive roots. There are phi(P-1) of them if the count transfers.
errors: Logical gap: the count phi(P-1) of proper cases is computed for 'abstract' roots. It transfers to residues mod P only if each x^d - 1 with d | P-1 has exactly d roots mod P. That follows from x^d - 1 dividing x^{P-1} - 1 together with Lagrange's bound (at most deg roots mod a prime). Euler does not argue it on this page, and his recursion over all divisors silently presupposes it. 'At most d' alone does not make the inclusion-exclusion exact. This is the weakness Gauss (Disq. Arith., around art. 56) points to in Euler's proof.
The general formula is only inferred inductively from the table ('vnde colligimus'), not proved. The multiplicativity of the recursion's solution is not demonstrated.

Typographical garble in the x^{ααβ} row: the printed intermediate expression ('ααβ − αα + α − (β−1)(β·1) − α − β + 1') does not literally equal the right-hand side. The correct computation is ααβ − [1 + (α−1) + α(α−1) + (β−1) + (α−1)(β−1)] = α(α−1)(β−1). The final result is correct.

ideas.what: Recursive count of roots of x^n - 1 not belonging to lower divisors, yielding sum_{d|n} N(d) = n and N(n) = phi(n)
ideas.modern_name: Gauss's identity sum_{d|n} phi(d) = n; number of primitive n-th roots of unity / degree of cyclotomic polynomial
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae art. 39 (1801) for the identity; phi itself to Euler (E271, 1763)
ideas.where_published: This paper, E449, Novi Comm. Acad. Petrop. 18 (1774); phi introduced in E271

ideas.what: Multiplicative formula phi(alpha^lambda beta^mu ...) = product of alpha^{lambda-1}(alpha-1)
Existence of elements of order P-1 mod P by counting elements of each order dividing P-1
ideas.modern_name: Existence of primitive roots via counting elements of order d (standard textbook proof)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler 1774 (gap), first rigorous: Legendre/Gauss (Gauss DA arts. 52-55)

missed.claim: Euler's recursion here already contains the divisor-sum identity sum_{d|n} phi(d) = n, 27 years before Gauss art. 39. Standard attributions credit Gauss and may not note this Euler precedent. The precedent is known to historians who discuss Euler's primitive-root proof (e.g. Sandifer), so it is only a minor attribution nuance.
missed.quote: tot dari casus proprios, quot infra exponentem n dantur numeri ad ipsum primi
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Attribution of an elementary identity; marginal.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is Euler's well-known (and well-critiqued) primitive-root argument. Its implicit sum_{d|n} phi(d) = n is a mild priority point but discussed in the historical literature on E449.
transcription_corrections: x^{ααβ} row: the image shows '−(β−1)(β·1)', a misprint in the original. The transcription's '(β−1)(β−1)' does not reflect a meaningful expression; the intended terms are −(β−1) −(α−1)(β−1).
General formula: the image shows γ^{ν−r} (printing artifact). It should read γ^{ν−1}, as the transcription correctly has.
